name: Parithiappar Temple, Tiruparidhiniyamam
deity: Shiva as Parithiappar (Bhaskareswarar, the sun-lord), with the goddess Mangalambikai (Mangalanayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Parithiappar Koil, the Tevaram's Tiruparidhiniyamam, near Thanjavur, honours Shiva as Parithiappar — also Bhaskareswarar, both names meaning the sun — with the goddess Mangalambikai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by all three great saints, Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, it is a sun shrine where Surya himself stands worshipping before the lingam.

sections.history: Parithiappar Koil, whose Tevaram name is Tiruparidhiniyamam (Parithi Niyamam), lies about 16–19 km from Thanjavur, on the road toward Pattukottai, in the Orathanadu taluk of Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by all three of the great saints — Tirugnana Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. The town was the home of Paridhi, one of the medieval commentators on the Tirukkural.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the delta, the shrine enshrines Parithiappar — also Bhaskareswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Mangalambikai, also Mangalanayaki, in her own shrine. Distinctively, the sun-god Surya is shown standing in worship before the lingam in the main shrine, and the temple has three Chandikeswarar images in its prakara, a rare feature.
sections.legends: Both the Tamil name Parithi and the Sanskrit Bhaskara mean the sun, and the shrine is above all a sun-temple: here Surya himself is said to have worshipped Shiva, and his standing image before the lingam keeps that devotion ever present. To worship the lord who was adored by the sun is held to bring light and auspiciousness into the devotee's life, under the grace of Mangalambikai, 'the mother of all good.'
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), the Suryapuja days when the light favours the lingam, Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Thanjavur include Parithiappar Koil among their stops.
sections.experience: At Parithiappar Koil the pilgrim comes to a shrine of the sun, where Surya stands worshipping before Shiva. Before Parithiappar, the sun-lord, and the all-auspicious Mangalambikai, with the three Chandikeswarars keeping watch, the visitor feels the warmth of a Tevaram temple sung by all three saints and blessed by the light itself.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Parithiappar Koil is about 16–19 km from Thanjavur on the road toward Pattukottai, in the Orathanadu taluk of Thanjavur district (PIN 614904). Thanjavur is the nearest major rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
